features.name: max_distinct_link_domains_per_comment
features.definition: What is the largest number of distinct source domains linked within any single counter-argument comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; missing/malformed -> null; empty list -> 0. For each comment, extract URLs with regex r'https?://[^\s)\]>]+' (also markdown link targets), take hostname lowercased, strip leading 'www.', and count distinct hostnames (exact hostname after www removal; no registered-domain collapsing). Return the maximum over comments. Raw text matching only; no semantic filtering.

features.name: any_comment_links_three_plus_domains
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment include links to 3 or more distinct source domains?
features.spec: df['max_distinct_link_domains_per_comment'] >= 3 as 0/1; null if df['max_distinct_link_domains_per_comment'] is null; 0 for an empty comment list.

h0: any_comment_links_three_plus_domains has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Rows with a counter-argument linking 3 or more distinct domains have a higher rate of OP view change than rows without.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Ambiguity: the threshold is applied within a single comment (a comment citing 3+ distinct domains), not pooled across comments. Domains are exact hostnames minus 'www' (assumption). Links are only about 12% of rows, so the feature will be sparse. Only current text is available, so URLs may appear in comments after or alongside the outcome; no timing is known. Raw URL detection does not check that links are evidence or whether they are quoted. OC_comments only; conversation is not used.
